subject.title: Telegram: unquarantine skipped sticker e2e tests

question: Should Telegram maintainers require a dedicated static WEBP sticker metadata e2e test, or accept the current cache-refresh, lower-level download, and runtime sticker-media coverage as sufficient?
rationale: Current main only partially satisfies the original unskip criteria, and the protected maintainer/product-decision labels mean automation should not decide the remaining coverage bar.

options.title: Restore one static WEBP e2e test
options.body: Add a narrow deterministic e2e case for the static WEBP sticker metadata path while keeping the existing cache-refresh test active.

options.title: Accept current coverage and close
options.body: Document that lower-level static download coverage plus the active cache-refresh e2e case are enough, then close this issue without adding another e2e test.

recommendation.title: Restore one static WEBP e2e test
recommendation.body: Add a narrow deterministic e2e case for the static WEBP sticker metadata path while keeping the existing cache-refresh test active.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the stabilization PR that quarantined the tests and created the follow-up criteria, making them the clearest routing owner for the coverage decision.
